items.title: The Grounds of Attribution: Evidence, Rival Explanations, and What Can Be Credited in AI
items.abstract: The Grounds of Attribution: Evidence, Rival Explanations, and What Can Be Credited in AI is a conceptual research paper in the On Human Modeling series examining the evidential and institutional conditions of justified attribution in artificial intelligence. It distinguishes four kinds of attribution: a statement credited to a source, a capacity to a machine, a meaning to a signal, and an effect to an intervention. Each requires evidence that favors the proposed attribution over its strongest plausible rival explanation. Four principal records demonstrate the application of this standard. Judicial proceedings in London and New York distinguish source authenticity from support for an attributed proposition and established citation defects from evidence of AI involvement. The 2018 fatal automated vehicle collision in Tempe distinguishes successful object detection from classification, trajectory prediction, and effective collision avoidance within a particular operating configuration. Independent evaluations of the Epic Sepsis Model distinguish predictive ranking, threshold performance, warning time, and clinical benefit. A randomized clinical trial involving 15,965 patients in Taiwan found estimated 90-day mortality of 3.6% among patients assigned to an AI-enabled electrocardiography alert workflow, compared with 4.3% under usual care. The individual contributions of model selection, alert delivery, and physician response remain unmeasured. Drawing on six entries from the 361-entry Matrix of Relations, the paper develops a five-step attribution procedure: specify the claim, identify the strongest ordinary rival, locate discriminating evidence, narrow the claim where necessary, and establish who can act on the distinction before reliance. It separates claims about the model, the people using it, and their combined system. Proposed institutional repairs extend to source verification, automated system release, threshold-based decisions, and component attribution. The contribution is a general framework for AI evaluation, epistemic accountability, and justified reliance. It distinguishes testing an attribution from testing the effectiveness of the procedure used to assess it. The proposed repairs remain untested. The central argument is that uncertainty about one attribution need not prevent warranted conclusions about others, provided that the evidence, its limits, and the authority to act on it are kept distinct.

items.title: The Human Intelligence, Data Analytics, Economics Behind AI
items.abstract: This paper examines the economic value of human intelligence behind modern artificial intelligence systems. While AI is frequently analyzed through technical capabilities and hardware infrastructure, its foundation relies heavily on accumulated human knowledge, research, software development, and daily digital interactions. By conceptualizing AI as an economic production system, this study explores the relationship between human labor, data acquisition, computing power, energy, and infrastructure. Furthermore, it highlights the global imbalance between countries that supply human knowledge and those that own the commercial AI infrastructure, warning of a new form of economic dependency for developing nations like Pakistan. The paper concludes by advocating for objective data analytics frameworks to measure human knowledge contributions and strategic investments in local technological ecosystems.

items.title: The Human Side of AI Education: Teacher Mediation, Student Self-Regulation, and Equitable Outcomes—A Sequential Explanatory Mixed-Methods Study in Secondary Education
items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into secondary education presents a critical paradox: tools designed to personalize learning may simultaneously undermine the cognitive autonomy and self-regulatory agency essential for deep learning. This study investigates the mediating role of teacher pedagogical mediation in shaping the relationship between GenAI-supported personalized learning and student outcomes—specifically, self-regulated learning (SRL), critical thinking, and equitable participation. Grounded in the Teacher-Mediated AI Regulation (T-MAIR) framework and Self-Determination Theory, this research employs a sequential explanatory mixed-methods design across three socioeconomically contrasting secondary school contexts in Dera Ismail Khan, Pakistan. Phase One (quantitative) tests a mediated moderation model through structural equation modeling with a stratified sample of 600–800 students and 60–80 teachers. Phase Two (qualitative) employs classroom observations, teacher interviews, and student focus groups to explain and contextualize quantitative findings. This study addresses a critical gap in the literature: while AI's technical capabilities are well documented, the pedagogical conditions under which AI supports rather than undermines equitable, autonomous learning remain insufficiently theorized and empirically tested. Findings will contribute a validated mediation model, a teacher mediation competency framework, and evidence-based policy recommendations for equitable AI integration.

items.title: The Impact of AI-Powered Financial Recommendations and Trust in Artificial Intelligence on Investment Intention Among University Students in Indonesia
items.abstract: This study aims to examine the effects of AI-powered financial recommendations and trust in artificial intelligence on investment intention among university students in Indonesia. A quantitative research approach was employed using questionnaire data collected from 143 respondents. The study investigates two independent variables, namely AI-powered financial recommendations and trust in artificial intelligence, with investment intention as the dependent variable. Data were analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation analysis, reliability testing, heteroskedasticity testing, and multiple linear regression. The results indicate that trust in artificial intelligence has a positive and statistically significant relationship with investment intention across the reported regression models. AI-powered financial recommendations also demonstrate a positive relationship with investment intention, although their statistical significance varies across model specifications. Furthermore, the reliability coefficients for all research variables exceed 0.80, indicating satisfactory internal consistency. The Breusch–Pagan/Cook–Weisberg test reveals no evidence of heteroskedasticity. These findings suggest that trust in artificial intelligence is an important factor associated with students' investment intention, while AI-powered financial recommendations may also contribute to their willingness to invest. items.title: THE IMPACT OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE ON ORGANIZATIONAL PERFORMANCE: A SIX-YEAR SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF HR LITERATURE
items.abstract: The growing integration of Digital Transformation (DT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping Human Resources (HR) practices and modern organizational structures. This study presents a systematic literature review examining the impact of DT and AI on Organizational Performance (OP) over a six-year period (2020–2025). Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) guidelines, data were extracted from the Scopus database. An initial pool of 155 records was sequentially filtered by subject area, document type, and language to 70 eligible articles, and then refined through qualitative full-text screening to a final corpus of 63 peer-reviewed research articles. The corpus was analyzed using a hybrid methodology combining textometric analysis via IRAMUTEQ and bibliometric network mapping via VOSviewer. The findings indicate that data science and AI positively influence multidimensional OP. Rather than being marginalized by automation, the HR function emerges as a socio-technical architect and strategic catalyst, aligning algorithmic capabilities with human capital. Theoretically, this review identifies persistent gaps and highlights the need to examine moderating variables such as organizational culture, resistance to change, and ethical leadership. Managerially, it suggests that sustaining competitive advantage depends on structural agility and responsible algorithmic governance. Finally, this study calls for future research to test these global theoretical models within the institutional and socioeconomic realities of emerging economies—particularly the Moroccan context—to better understand how local dynamics shape technology adoption and organizational efficiency. Keywords: Digitalization; Digital transformation; Artificial Intelligence; Human resource management; Organizational performance; Systematic literature review.

items.title: The impact of generative artificial intelligence supported project based language learning on EFL speaking proficiency among Chinese undergraduates
items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) into Project-Based Language Learning (PBLL), an approach in which learners use the target language to complete meaningful projects toward a defined outcome, remains underexplored, especially for English Language Learning (EFL) speaking development in China. This study examined the relationship between GenAI-integrated PBLL (GenAI-PBLL) and Chinese EFL undergraduates’ speaking proficiency and explored their perceptions of the intervention. Using a quasi-experimental, explanatory sequential mixed-methods design, 78 Chinese undergraduates from two intact classes participated in a 10-week intervention: 39 received GenAI-PBLL instruction and 39 received teacher-led traditional instruction. Quantitative data were collected using the College English Test–Spoken English Test Band 4 (CET-SET 4) and an EFL speaking self-perceived improvement scale, followed by semi-structured interviews with 10 experimental group undergraduates. A mixed-design ANOVA showed a significant Time × Group interaction, indicating that the experimental group demonstrated greater improvement in overall speaking proficiency than the control group. Qualitative findings further indicated positive learner perceptions of GenAI-PBLL. Theoretically, the study extends the application of a Zone of Proximal Development (ZPD)-informed perspective to GenAI-supported PBLL. Practically, the findings suggest that GenAI can be integrated into project-based speaking activities to provide linguistic support, idea generation and feedback, while maintaining teacher guidance, peer collaboration, and learner-generated oral production.

items.title: The Importance of Artificial Intelligence in Modern Software Systems: A Review and Descriptive Survey of Computing Students
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become an integral component of contemporary software products, development workflows, and system operations, while raising concerns about reliability, security, and responsible use. This paper reviews these contributions and challenges and presents descriptive survey findings from 159 computing students. The survey covered AI exposure and usage, ten five-point Likert items on perceived importance and benefits, ten items on perceived challenges, and three open-ended questions. The reported overall simple mean was 3.99 out of 5 for perceived benefits (SD = 1.06) and 3.58 for perceived challenges (SD = 1.08). Debugging assistance (M = 4.14), conceptual understanding (M = 4.13), and faster coding (M = 4.08) were the highest-rated benefits. Unreliable AI output (M = 3.98) and possible weakening of problem-solving skills (M = 3.85) were leading concerns. These findings suggest that respondents value AI as a learning and development aid while recognizing a need for verification, independent judgment, and responsible integration. Because the survey is cross-sectional, self-reported, and confined to a single institution, the results describe this group rather than establish causal or population-wide effects.

items.title: The mechanism by which facilitating conditions affect university teachers’ behavioral intention to use GenAI through a chain mediation analysis based on the technology acceptance model
items.abstract: The association between facilitating conditions (FC) and behavioral intention (BI) to use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) among university teachers was investigated by empirical analysis using a structural equation model based on the extended technology acceptance model (TAM), with a sample of 315 university teachers in Anhui. Because the data were collected cross-sectionally, the study is correlational in design, and the serial mediation model reported here represents a theoretically hypothesized pathway rather than an empirically verified causal sequence. The results showed that facilitating conditions were significantly associated with teachers’ behavioral intention to use GenAI by university teachers, both directly and indirectly. Meanwhile, perceived ease of use (PE) was strongly associated with behavioral intention and with perceived usefulness (PU); a chain mediation pattern of “facilitating conditions → perceived ease of use → perceived usefulness → behavioral intention” was consistent with the data. Convergent and discriminant validity were supported by composite reliability, average variance extracted and both the Fornell–Larcker and HTMT criteria, and a comparison of a one-factor and a four-factor model indicated that a single general factor could not account for the covariance among the items. This study expands the applicability of TAM in the context of GenAI for this teacher population, thereby providing theoretical and practical references for digital transformation of university education and artificial intelligence literacy of university teachers.

items.title: The Mediating Role of AI Literacy in Students' Adoption of Artificial Intelligence Tools: An Extended Technology Acceptance Model Approach
items.abstract: The rapid expansion of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in higher education has increased the need to understand the factors influencing students' adoption of these technologies. This paper examines the mediating role of AI literacy (AIL) in the relationships between perceived usefulness (PU), perceived ease of use, knowledge sharing, and students' behavioral intention (BI) to use AI tools for learning within the technology acceptance model framework. A quantitative cross-sectional survey was conducted with 267 undergraduate students at a public university in Saudi Arabia, and the data were analyzed using covariance-based structural equation modeling (AMOS). The results indicate that PU and perceived ease of use significantly predict BI, while PU and knowledge sharing significantly predict AIL. AIL also positively influences BI. The findings highlight the important role of AIL in supporting students' effective adoption of AI tools in higher education.

items.title: The mediating role of intrinsic job motivation in the relationship between perceived job autonomy and turnover intention among administrative university employees in Norway: findings from 2020 to 2023
items.abstract: Background Previous research has demonstrated a heterogeneity of associations between perceived job autonomy and Turnover Intention (TI), often implying underlying mechanisms. This study addresses this gap by providing novel insight into the mediating role of intrinsic job motivation in the relationship between job autonomy and TI among administrative university staff from the COVID-19 outbreak to the post-pandemic period. Thus, the objective of this study is to (1) describe job autonomy, intrinsic job motivation and TI from 2020 to 2023 among administrative employees and to (2) explore the mediating role of intrinsic job motivation in the relationship between perceived job autonomy and TI. Methods Annual cross-sectional aggregated data from the ARK-questionnaire, collected between 2020 and 2023, were administered. In total, 11,496 administrative employees participated during this period. The survey was electronically distributed by email. All procedures and questions had received approval from the Norwegian Agency for Shared Services in Education and Research (SIKT). Mediation analyses were conducted in SPSS version 30 for Mac, using PROCESS macro by Hayes. Results Across the period 2020 to 2023, job autonomy among Norwegian administrative employees was high and showed a slight upward trend (mean = 4.06 to 4.14 from 2020 to 2023). Intrinsic job motivation remained relatively stable (mean = 3.70 to 3.75), while turnover intention was generally low, with some variation over time (mean = 2.11 to 2.16). Mediation analyses demonstrated that intrinsic job motivation partially mediated the relationship between job autonomy and TI with progressively higher proportions of indirect effects across years. Notably, in 2023, intrinsic job motivation mediated this relationship, indicating that TI appeared to operate primarily through its impact on intrinsic job motivation. Conclusions This study provides evidence that job autonomy influences turnover intention through its effect on intrinsic job motivation. These findings underscore the importance of fostering work environments to strengthen intrinsic job motivation and thereby reduce employees' intentions to leave. Together, these insights contribute to a better understanding of turnover dynamics after COVID-19 and emphasize the need for organizational practices that support intrinsic job motivation rather than autonomy alone for employee retention.

items.title: The Mediating Role of Prompt Quality in AI-Assisted Academic Writing: A Serial Mediation Model Among Linguistically Diverse Students
items.abstract: Generative Artificial Intelligence (Gen-AI) tools are increasingly adopted by university students for academic writing tasks. However, limited empirical evidence exists regarding how students' prompt quality and cognitive load reduction mediate the relationship between Gen-AI features and academic writing outcomes, particularly among linguistically diverse learners. A convergent mixed-methods design was employed. Quantitative data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of 815 linguistically diverse university students from seven higher education institutions in China. Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) was used to test the hypothesised serial mediation model. Qualitative data were collected through semi-structured interviews with 30 participants and analysis of 300 authentic prompts from their AI interactions. All five Gen-AI affordances positively influenced prompt quality (β = .358–.418, all p < .001) and cognitive load reduction. Prompt quality significantly mediated the relationship between Gen-AI affordances and cognitive load reduction. Cognitive load reduction significantly mediated the relationship between prompt quality and both academic resilience (β = .275) and personalised learning (β = .287). Serial mediation analyses confirmed the pathway: Gen-AI affordances, Prompt Quality, Cognitive Load Reduction, and Academic Outcomes. Qualitative findings revealed four key themes: (1) prompt crafting as a learned skill, (2) contextual factors influencing prompt quality, (3) iterative refinement strategies, and (4) barriers to effective prompting, including language proficiency and lack of training. Gen-AI tools can support academic writing by reducing cognitive burden, but only when students craft high-quality prompts. This study clarifies the mediating role of prompt quality and cognitive processes, offering practical implications for educators, students, and EdTech developers.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PEOPLE'S MANAGEMENT IN ORGANIZATIONS FOR DRIVING SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT IN EMERGING ECONOMIES
items.abstract: This paper explores the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI), People Management—traditionally termed Human Resource Management (HRM)—and Sustainable Development within the context of emerging economies. Emerging markets face distinct structural challenges, including infrastructure gaps, high youth unemployment, institutional voids, and economic volatility. By deploying AI tools to automate routine tasks, reduce human bias in recruitment, personalize professional development, and monitor worker well-being, businesses can cultivate resilient environments that support long-term economic, social, and environmental sustainability. However, risks such as algorithmic discrimination, deep data privacy concerns, and the widening digital divide pose significant implementation barriers. This paper provides a detailed, highly scannable analysis demonstrating how an ethical, human-centric AI model in people management can serve as a powerful engine to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)

items.title: TRANSFORMATION OF LEGAL REGULATION OF ROBOTIC COMPLEXES IN THE CONDITIONS OF INDUSTRY 4.0: COLLISIONS OF TECHNICAL AND LEGAL NORMS
items.abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive theoretical and legal analysis of the transformation in the regulation of industrial robotic systems (IRS) driven by Industry 4.0 technologies. It explores the phenomenon of "technical law," wherein traditional legislative acts are increasingly superseded by harmonized engineering standards. The study identifies key conflicts between existing civil, commercial, and labor law norms and the specific characteristics of modern cyber-physical production systems. It analyzes the legal status of IRS, specifically the distinction between a "machine" and "partly completed machinery," as well as the issue of shifting liability boundaries during system integration. Particular attention is given to collaborative robotics ("cobots"), the integration of artificial intelligence algorithms, and the convergence of industrial safety and cybersecurity, as addressed in EU Regulation 2023/1230 and the updated ISO 10218 standard series. Finally, the paper offers proposals for modernizing Ukrainian legislation and adapting state regulatory mechanisms.

items.title: Translational artificial intelligence in therapeutic-era metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: The ACTION framework
items.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) has entered a therapeutic era in which priorities extend beyond detecting steatosis to identifying treatment-actionable fibrosis, rationalising referral and biopsy, standardising trial endpoints and monitoring response. Artificial intelligence (AI) spans electronic health records, non-invasive tests, imaging and digital pathology, but reports often omit the user, threshold and consequence. We conducted a structured narrative review and developed the author-proposed ACTION framework. ACTION comprises attached action, calibration in context, threshold-specific benefit, integration, oversight, and non-discrimination and monitoring. Evidence is uneven. Case-finding and enrichment models can identify uncoded or higher-risk patients, but their prospective effects on testing, referral and outcomes remain unproven. Imaging AI supports reproducible quantification, although signals may add little beyond clinical variables. The human-reviewed AI-based measurement tool for MASH (in regulatory records) is among the most mature applications reviewed, within a narrowly specified clinical-trial context. It is qualified for specified MASH clinical-trial workflows, not for autonomous diagnosis or unrestricted treatment selection. AI becomes clinically meaningful only when a calibrated output is linked to a predefined action, an accountable human user and a measurable patient or trial outcome.

items.title: Uneven Alignment of Artificial Intelligence Research in the Food Industry with Industry 5.0: A Bibliometric and Text-Mining Study
items.abstract: Research on artificial intelligence in the food industry is growing rapidly, but its attention to the human-centered, sustainable and resilient principles of Industry 5.0 remains unclear. This study examines 3,137 publications on artificial intelligence in the food industry and related supply chains, indexed in Scopus and Web of Science from 2018 to October 2026. Bibliometric analysis, topic modelling and dictionary-based text mining were used to analyze publication trends, research topics and eleven technology-related, organizational and human-centered themes, and the results were checked under alternative selection and classification rules. Publications grew by about 57% annually, and technical applications dominate. Attention to trust, governance, adoption and explainability rose to 9–16% of recent publications, whereas human-centricity (2.3%), workforce and skills (3.8%) and small and medium-sized enterprises (1.9%, declining) remained underrepresented, and agentic artificial intelligence emerged only in 2025. Human-centered themes were generally positively associated with emerging technologies, indicating that the main imbalance is limited research volume rather than missing thematic connections. The literature therefore shows uneven alignment with Industry 5.0 principles.
